Interface generation (formerly US-037): when --no-interface is NOT passed, rt refactor convert-static-class generates an I<TypeName>.cs file in the same folder containing the extracted public/internal instance method and property signatures.

Interface generation: the generated I<TypeName> interface declares the same accessibility as the source class (public for public, internal for internal) and is added to the workspace as a new document.
Interface generation: the converted class declares `: I<TypeName>` in its base list with correct whitespace and brace placement (no `IDisposable\n,IFoo{` style malformations).
Interface generation: each public/internal instance method on the converted class implements the interface signature 1:1; private methods and fields are excluded.
Interface generation: --no-interface flag suppresses interface file creation and base list update; only the class itself is destatified.

DI registration (formerly US-038): when --no-di-registration is NOT passed, the command locates Bootstrap.RegisterServices(IServiceCollection services) in the solution and inserts services.AddSingleton<I<TypeName>, <TypeName>>() (or the configured lifetime).
DI registration: --lifetime singleton|scoped|transient flag selects the registration shape; default is singleton.
DI registration: when no Bootstrap.RegisterServices method is found in the solution, the command emits a warning to stderr and skips DI registration without failing the run.
DI registration: when the registration line already exists, the command is idempotent — no duplicate line added.

Field and ctor formatting (formerly US-039): the AddConstructorInjection rewrite places the injected field on its own line with the correct trailing newline; it does NOT merge with the existing first member.

Field and ctor formatting: when the consumer class already has constructors, the new field/parameter pair is inserted with consistent indentation (4 spaces) matching the existing constructor formatting.
Field and ctor formatting: the constructor parameter list is wrapped to one parameter per line when adding to a class that already uses one-per-line wrapping; otherwise stays single-line.
Dry-run (--dry-run) emits a unified diff showing: interface file creation, class signature change, DI registration line addition, and any ctor/field rewrites.

rt refactor convert-static-class src/RoslynTools/Core/SymbolFormatter.cs --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run produces output that, when applied, results in a buildable solution (verified by piping the dry-run apply through dotnet build).

Integration test fixture covers: (a) static class with no consumers — interface + DI registration only; (b) static class with one consumer using empty ctor — both consumer rewrite paths; (c) static class with one consumer using existing ctor — exercises the field/formatting path from US-039; (d) --no-interface and --no-di-registration flags.
